Review Text:
Our helicopter tour was great.

We were fortunate that the weather was about perfect; sunny, low 70s with hardly any wind.
The copter we were in had 8 seats, 4 in front and 4 in the second row. Seats are assigned (I think by weight) with 3 passengers (plus the pilot) in front and 4 passengers in the second row.
It was warm in the copter even with air conditioning.
Base on our experience it seems like the best views (although there a no bad views) are from the right side.
We appreciated the narration and explanations provided by our pilot.
We were a little surprised by the bumpiness of the ride related to the force of the chopper blades, but it is not the kind of movement that would cause motion sickness.

Review Title: What a fabulous experience - Bucket list item ticked off
Review Text:
Easy check in process when we arrived at reception where you have to get weighed so they know where to seat you on the helicopter. The waiting room has plenty of comfy seats and large windows so you can see the other helicopters coming in and out.
Our pilot (didn't catch his name) had a great sense of humour and helped us all relax so we could enjoy our flight. You don't get to choose where to sit on the helicopter as its all done by weight, but there were 3 passenger seats in the front plus the pilot and 3 seats in the back.
Our 50 minute flight was amazing and went really quickly. Great views of the Canyon and the surrounding area. Once landed we had plenty of time for photos next to the helicopter and the pilot. Its an expensive experience but so worth doing and something to tick off your bucket list.

Review Title: Experience the sheer size of GC
Review Text: There’s a nice spacious area to wait and parking outside. You can’t take any baggage so leave it in your car. There’s a shop and vending machine but no coffee. The pilot was Dave, a lovely young man and experienced pilot who truly loves the GC. He gave us great information and was very friendly. You need to be weighed on arrival ( it’s discrete) and you are sat in the helicopter where they want to balance it. There are 8 seats inside with 3 in front next to the pilot and 4 behind. It isn’t bumpy and lurching - although there are a few twists and tips. It’s just exciting. It’s not like rollercoaster stunt flying, it’s very smooth really, and I was pleased I didn’t feel at all travel sick.i know it’s a costly trip, but it’s really worth it. The very best way to see some of the Grand Canyon.

Review Text:
We did the 45 minute tour and it was one of the best things we have ever done. It is by far the best way to appreciate the scale of the canyon.

The seating in the chopper is set by the computer based on the weight of all passengers in order to achieve a good balance, so there is no point worrying about where you will sit (you simply can’t control it). All the views were good though.

The seats are small so if you are on the larger side you may want to book two. I think they say the chopper technically seats 7 (with pilot) but it would be cramped with over 5 adults.

Forrest our pilot did an excellent job pointing things out and giving us a bit of history/info. Review Title: Best Way to See the Grand Canyon
Review Text: This was definitely the way to see the Grand Canyon and worth the cost to do the longer ride (some options only offer 25 minutes—that wouldn't have been enough). Maverick helicopters was efficient and well-organized.  There were 6 people plus the pilot in our helicopter. They assigned us our seats based on weight distribution, so no choice there.  Taking good photos was a bit problematic because of window glare and wherever you happened to be seated in the cabin.  But the photos were good enough to keep the memory alive.  Our pilot was informative and engaging.  We felt very safe and lucky to be able to do the ride.  We were a little chagrined to see when we got there that walk-in tickets were about $30 or so cheaper than we paid through Tripadvisor. Review Title: Another item checked off the bucket list
Review Text: My Canyon Spirit  helicopter tour was part of a 2200 mile motor trip including Zion, Bryce, Monument Valley and Page.  The decision to view the Grand Canyon by air instead of hiking did not disappoint.  The weather for my 9 15 am flight was clear and calm and fellow passengers included a father/son from Germany and a senior couple from Wisconsin – all of whom were very excited for the flight.  The most amusing part of the trip was when our handsome pilot, John Paul, told us his favourite parts of the Grand Canyon after piloting the Canyon trips for a mere 5 days. As the audio briefly cut out all we heard was he had flown helicopters for 5 days !  Too funny!  (he formerly worked at the Las Vegas location)  The journey was smooth and gentle – like a flying couch – which is critical to those of us who suffer from motion sickness.  The temperature inside the helicopter was perfect – having been baked on stifling flights over Niagara Falls, Ontario, Canada and Canmore, Alberta, Canada,  I was pleased the pilot confirmed our comfort level several times.  The views are spectacular:  full of colour and texture.  Some passengers are interested in photography, others are content to soak up the views.  The richness of any experience is determined by what you bring to it – asking a few questions of the pilot who flies tourists over the Canyon every day brought a whole different perspective to the Grand Canyon experience.  For those of us not paying in US dollars its pricey but as a once in a lifetime flight it was worth it.  (And for ‘balance’ reasons I got to sit next to the pilot – it was tough but someone had to do it)

Review Title: The Wonder of the GC, and a great aerial photo shoot
Review Text:
My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed the ride and pilot Eddie. Very smooth ride at 7500-9500 feet which can be below the canyon rim at times. Excellent for taking aerial photos. The rear seats may be even better for photos as it has flatter plexiglass. I usually shoot open window from a plane, the plexiglass did not introduce distortion. Photos taken shutter priority 1/1000sec. f4.5, Typically 70-100mm. A wider lens 24-70mm would have been good as well. You don't need extreme telephoto.

About an hour through the ZUNI and DRAGON corridors (see GREEN route 1). Desolate territory although we saw a raft and people below.

Fantastic way to see a small part of this immense natural wonder. Both of us were very happy for the opportunity. Sights around each corner. If you use Google Earth search for KGCN for the airport.

Very professional staff, sharp looking waiting areas, utmost concern for peoples safety and comfort. Our pilot was using his checklist to go over the briefing he must have done hundreds of times to ensure he wouldn't miss anything

Review Title: Great Views Depending on Which Seats You Are Assigned
Review Text:
Maverick assigns your seats based on what other people are on the tour and weights of individual passengers. They arbitrarily combine couples or groups of passengers to each flight over the Canyon.

There are two seats in front by the pilot and there are four seats in the back. If you are fortunate enough to get the two seats in front beside the pilot or on the left rear behind the pilot, you will have amazing views. If you are assigned the two middle seats or the far right seat, forget getting to see much. The back right window is smaller and has obstructed views. Also, our pilot kept the orientation of the helicopter such that the right side was always away from the best views of the Canyon.

I would not waste my money again, since the arbitrarily seat assignment determines your views, or lack thereof.

Review Title: Just WOW - An Experience Like No Other!
Review Text: My family of 4 did this tour last week and were beyond impressed.  We opted for Maverick because of their fleet of newer helicopters with ample windows spanning down to the floor in the front.  Navigation to the airport and check in was so easy, with a relaxing space and gift shop to wait prior to the flight.  We chose the 45 minute flight because I don't know when my next opportunity will arise to take a helicopter tour, and I didn't regret this small upgrade in price.  We saw so much yet 45 minutes passed by quite quickly.  We travelled with our 7 and 10 year old children and were placed in a private tour with no others, which was wonderful and we all had a fantastic view, I was in front with the two kids and my husband was behind the pilot next to the window.  Our pilot Mark was phenomenal; very skilled in flying, knowledgeable on the geography of the Grand Canyon, and entertaining.  At no point were we nervous, even my 7 year old son, it was a very calm and amazing experience.  I was actually more nervous just walking on the trails into the canyon later that day rather than flying high over the canyon itself.  We never would have seen the Colorado River and some of the formations without taking this tour.  The only thing I would have prepped my kids with prior is that we were assigned seats once we got outside to the helicopter (they were happy and luckily we had no issues) and that once we're flying, we had to talk via the headsets.  I could tell my son started getting a little frustrated because he couldn't follow all of the pilot's information pointed out, but I was able to tell him to just relax and enjoy, there is no quiz afterwards, and he was much better after that just soaking in the sights.  You can't see the Grand Canyon like this any other way, it's such a unique experience and was well worth it.  It is an experience my family will remember forever.

I would highly recommend this trip to anyone considering it. The views are absolutely amazing - you wouldn't be able to see even half as much from ground level. The pilot acts as a tour guide, pointing out parts of the GC like the fault lines, the river, the Native American section etc.

Check-in process is simple and straight-forward - you need to arrive around 45 minutes in advance of the flight to check-in. There's a comfortable waiting area. You can't take any bags etc with you (you are able to take phones, cameras, water), but they check the bags in behind the front desk for you for no extra fee.

If you book through Trip Advisor they will need to see a 'payment voucher'. My email confirmation from TA sufficed.

Worth mentioning that you don't find out where you are sitting until you are there. We were lucky and ended up with front row seats. There are three front-row passenger seats, then four back-row passenger seats (two of which are window seats). I imagine this changes how much you are able to see. Our flight only had five people on it which we were told is the norm (it was peak time 12:45 in August).

Review Text:
My husband and I booked the Canyon Spirit, 45-50min tour with Maverick Helicopters as part of a 3 week tour around the west of America. We booked it online a month before we went through the chat option on their website, where they gave us a bit of a discount and all the information we needed.
We were told to book in advance because it gets so busy and booked up and we were really glad we did. We did a lot of research on the different options of people to fly with and it paid off because there's nothing we'd change about the one we did. It cost $544 for both of us, which is a lot of money but we'd totally recommend it.

We flew at 8am on Thursday September 15, 2018. It was a perfect time and day. The weather was amazing and it was all perfect for the flight. You have to get there about 30 mins before the flight and you're weighed so they can allocate you in the helicopter according to weight, to spread it out. You can't choose or request a specific seat. Fortunately my husband and I got to sit in the front and it was spectacular. The helicopter is largely glass and from the front you can see right down to take in the view. However, there is a great view from every seat and I really wouldn't worry about where you sit.

Each helicopter took 6 passengers, plus the pilot.

Everyone has headphones and a microphone so you can all communicate with one another during the flight and ask questions. We were fascinated by the number of helicopters that took off at similar times but yet once you're in the air and going over the canyon you can't see any at all. It felt like you were the only one in the air and it's very difficult to take in the sheer scale of the canyon even when you can see a lot of it.

There wasn't anything scary about it or unnerving, we absolutely loved our first trip in a helicopter.

We would thoroughly recommend this trip.

Review Title: This Should be on Your Bucket List
Review Text:
A very professionally run tourist operation, and a wonderfully informed and expansive pilot who managed the dual tasks of successfully keeping us aloft while deciphering and answering our inane and long-winded questions.
And coping with our infantile exclamations.
Yes, we were excited.
All of us.
My partner and I, and the 3 other passengers - a generational trio of grandmother, mother and daughter, all on their first helicopter flight.
We had a beautiful blue sky crisp winter morning for our tour.
That moment the chopper passed from the forested plateau over the rim of the canyon was, alone, worth the cost of the flight.
My mind was then scrambled by the sheer vastness of the canyon below and around us - the northern side is evidently higher than the southern side - and the breathtaking beauty of the canyon walls and formations, the colours, the light and the shadows.
And the teal green of the serpentine Colorado way down at the very bottom.
Time evaporated as we snaked along the river, rose above then flew over the northern rim - where we saw a herd of bison in a snow covered landscape - then re-entered the canyon further westward. I couldn't believe that we had been flying for as long as we had when we gently settled back on to the tarmac back at Maverick central.
Sensational, and a video of the flight available just in case you want to relive it.

It also helped to lift off to the Top Gun soundtrack, followed by a quality "mix tape" of classic rock gently pumped into our headsets as we soared over the landscape. The pilots knowledge of the area and delivery of the facts was as enjoyable as the ride itself. Outdone only by the views we experienced... I have never in all my days seen a landscape so beautiful.

Thank you Maverick Helicopters.

Review Text: This was by far the most breathtaking thing we did at they Grand Canyon. We hiked down 3 miles and did the entire rim, but to see so much of the canyon with such a knowledgeable guide was wonderful. We got our pictures taken in front of the chopper with the pilot before take off, and then climbed aboard the air conditioned craft. We each got a head set so we could listen to their perfectly timed background music while we asked questions or pointed out things below. We flew over the forest then  into the canyon, across both the Colorado and Little Colorado Rivers with our pilot telling us why they look different based on geology, then across the canyon to the North Rim with information on rock layers, names of peaks, information on rafting and the rapids, explorers, Native Americans, and more. We looped behind the visitor center of the North Rim (a no fly zone) and got to see wild bison below. Then back across the canyon towards the south rim for more breath taking views and over town to the airport. Our pilot was great and leaned forward out of my shot every time I pointed my camera at his window. He knew everything and was very friendly. I wish I had brought a polarized lens, as there was a bit of reflection in my pictures from the glare on the windows. My only complaint is that because they need to balance their chopper, I was not able to sit with my boyfriend for the 50 min ride, but could talk to him over the radio and did get a selfy with him behind me. My view in the front was much better than his in the back. The craft only fits 8 people, and we had 5 plus the pilot so we all got windows. I would love to do this again. Save up and go for it!

Review Title: A Once in a Lifetime - We Scored a Cracking Day!
Review Text:
Straight up, this is the single most expensive activity we did on our whole honeymoon. We debated long and hard if we could justify the cost, and researched the other operators offering similar service. We decided to go with Maverick due to their air-time and route being the most appealing we found. With all the travel we want to do around the world it is likely this would be our only visit here so we dug deep and coughed up the money as we know we'd regret if we didn't do it. We were not disappointed!

We knew there would be a few things that would have to go right for the best possible experience including the weather and our positions in the chopper. We came up trumps with both. We had a cracking day. No wind, so a smooth ride and excellent visibility. I can see people's frustration at being in the back row of the aircraft as you definitely get a better view up front and it is easier to take photos. (Though the bubble canopy makes photos without reflections tricky regardless of where you sit.) I had the good fortune of being the exact same weight as the pilot so I got a balancing seat opposite him with the little wifey sitting in the middle. The view from the back isn't terrible, but the front definitely gives the best experience. You just have to be lucky I suppose and I'm glad we were.

The Canyon was everything we hoped for and a chopper flight is easily the best way to experience it in a short period of time. We headed to the lookouts afterwards and there is simply no comparison. The pilot was skilled and the commentary informative. Every twist and turn unveiled a jaw-dropping panorama of river, rock and plateau. You spend the whole flight with a huge grin on your face and wondering if it is all real. The 45-minute flight felt sufficient and immersive, I think the shorter one would leave you wanting more. Due to the cost, I don't think I'd do it again, but you'll kick yourself if you don't do it once when you have the opportunity! It is truly a once-in-a-lifetime experience I don't think you can replicate anywhere else in the world. I thought our heli-flight back home over the Great Barrier Reef was amazing, this takes it to another level.

Review Title: Do it, don't regret not doing so!
Review Text:
When arranging our trip to the Grand Canyon we considered the options for add ons. Ultimately the only one we organised in advance was a helicopter flight. We did so because it was our first visit to the Grand Canyon and possibly the only one given all of the other places we have on our list to visit.

Having done our research we decided on Maverick Helicopters and chose the Canyon Spirit flight. Although a little more expensive than some flights (there are shorter flights) the time in the air was approximately 45 minutes.

It was also ideal as Maverick have a base at Grand Canyon Airport, Hwy 64, Grand Canyon just 5 minutes from where we were staying at the Best Western Grand Canyon enabling us to make best use of every minute of or trip.

When first booking we were advised by our travel company that a flight time couldn't be guaranteed. Despite that we expressed a preference for an early flight to hopefully capture the views in a good light and to enable the rest of the day for other exploration of the area. Nearer our departure we made contact with Maverick and learned that weather and all else permitting our flight would be the first of the day at 08:00 am and that we needed to be there 30 minutes before. We also phoned as requested the day before our flight to check in.

We arrived early on the day at 07:20 am and checked in. We were weighed as part of the process and then waited with anticipation.

Shortly before our flight our pilot Daniel, called or name out along with the remaining passenger - 6 in total leaving one seat empty. We were escorted out onto the tarmac where we had our photographs taken by Maverick in our individual family groups with the pilot before being allocated our seats and given a safety briefing. We assume seats were allocated on the basis of balancing the weight of the group but it avoided a free for all over who would sit where.

The ECO-Star (EC130) helicopter made by Airbus Helicopters was a eight seater - the pilot plus six passengers i.e. two rows of four.

My wife sat in the front next to the pilot and me behind him next to the window. That said every seat had a great view. As wearing headphones is necessary in order to communicate we were all able to interact with the pilot who gave a great commentary. The whole flight including audio was recorded using a camera mounted on the front of the helicopter meaning that those of us who wanted to could purchase a copy along with a nice plaque including the pre-flight photograph.

Following take off we departed from the Grand Canyon South Rim over the Kaibab National Forest before reaching the rim of the Canyon that dropped away before us ....... this really was a spectacular view and incredible feeling. Flying over the Canyon we could see for miles. The North rim and eastern edge then cam into view something that many visitors don't see and nor would we if it hadn't been for the flight. We then followed the Colorado River and were able to see the water flowing at the foot of the Canyon. Flying through the widest and deepest part of the Canyon we were able to take as many photographs as we liked and in my case GoPro footage of almost the entire flight.

Crossing the Colorado River we left the Grand Canyon and returned to base.

On landing and once it was safe to alight we were able to take our own photographs around the helicopter including with our pilot.

We then returned to the terminal building where those of us who wanted could purchase a DVD recording of the flight and or plaque with our pre-flight photograph as a memento. We don't ordinarily purchase such things but this was a very special experience so we can now relive it with friends and family.

We have some amazing memories and great photographs. It was an incredible, beautiful and absolutely awesome experience that we would highly recommend.

If you want to do this don't wait until it's too late plan ahead to be sure you can get a flight.

Special thanks go to Daniel our pilot for making our experience so good.

Review Title: Highly Recommended Once In A Lifetime Experience!

Review Text:
We decided on the Maverick Helicopter Tour as it seemed that they had newer equipment than the other tour companies in the area. You meet at the Tusayan Airport which is outside of the Grand Canyon National Park (It is just outside of Tusayan). They have a large parking lot and guest services building with a gift shop, vending machines and restrooms. Check-in is fast and easy. They do take your weight (no lying about your weight, as you actually stand on a scale) which they use to assign your seating on the helicopter to balance the weight. You can request a front seat but they cannot guarantee specific seating but will give you preference if you ask in advance. Once everyone is checked in the pilot will call out your name and give you a seat assignment. You are provided with a life preserver that you wear around your waist and are assisted in getting in the helicopter. Once in, you put on your headphones and get a quick safety check. (you should wear dark clothing without prints so that you don't get a reflection off the inside of the glass when you take photos). The flight is about 45 minutes and there are no restrooms on the helicopter and no stops until you get back to the airport (as my Mother always told me, go now or forever hold your pees). The seats are very comfortable (seating for 7 including the pilot) and the helicopter is surprisingly quiet from others I have flown in. The weather was clear and the flight very calm and smooth.

Once everyone is secure the pilot takes off and introduces himself and finds out a little bit about you. You initially fly over the pine forests and listen to a play list and commentary through your headphones. Then you fly out over the Canyon itself. The view is spectacular as the trees and land immediately end and fall away from view and you are now hovering 4,000 feet above the Canyon Floor! The pilot forewarned us just before we cleared the trees and got our first panoramic view of the Canyon but it is still breathtaking! The pilot describes the various areas of the Canyon and sights and flies along both the South and North Rims as well as along the Colorado River. You can ask questions through your headsets and the pilot is more than happy to respond and elaborate on his narration. Although we viewed the Canyon from the South Rim, the Rim Trails, the Bright Angel Trail and the West Rim, this is a unique "not to miss" way to see the Canyon if your budget allows.

After about 45 minutes we landed back at the airport and they took pictures of us by the helicopter (with or without the pilot) and using their camera and ours. Although not required or requested, we did give a small gratuity to the pilot which I'm sure he appreciated. When we got back into the gift shop they had photos on the wall that you could purchase as well as a dvd of your specific flight made during the actual flight. Unfortunately the camera on our helicopter malfunctioned on our flight so we couldn't purchase the dvd of our flight but because we had asked to buy the dvd they gave us a complimentary copy of their generic dvd of the helicopter flight (very considerate and professional).

The price for the helicopter flight was about $300 per person for about 45 minutes but was well worth it. If you want to get a different perspective of the Grand Canyon, this is definitely not a tour to miss! I would highly recommend both the helicopter flight and Maverick Helicopters as the tour provider.

Review Title: A genuine highlight, but not stress free! - July 11th 2015
Review Text:
Sorry - this is a long review, but there is some constructive feedback at the end which needs reading.

Having booked with Maverick airlines last year to fly from Vegas to the South Rim on a small plane tour, one regret was not taking up the option of a helicopter flight. This year my wife, daughter and I had planned another road trip but coming at the Canyon from a different direction - on the train from Williams.

My first interaction with Maverick was by live chat on their website in February '15. Spoke to a lady called Elaine who was helpful and informative. My big question: the train arrives at 11:45am and leaves at 3.15pm - what would be the best option for a 40 minute Canyon Spirit tour? She suggested the 12:45 flight, with 12:15 check in. It would be 20 minutes in a cab from the train depot so plenty of time. No they don't have their own transport but cabs would be readily available and she gave me the number to call one in advance.

I wanted more time to think it through before booking and it was May before I felt confident to reserve 3 seats on Saturday the 11th July at 12:45. Maverick advised me that we were the only 3 on the flight and that they'd need at least 3 more before they'd fly. Same instruction as last year - call the day before to check in and confirm the flight.

Our holiday itinerary meant we'd be on the road a lot during office hours. I called Maverick from San Diego 2 days before to confirm and they told me they had still not sold any other seats but not to worry, they usually do. 12 hours later we were in Williams with the train the next morning. Called again - yes they had enough seats sold so the flight would go ahead.

At this point I started worrying about the taxi. I called the phone number to book one. Unobtainable. I googled cabs in the Grand Canyon, but only Flagstaff numbers came up. Just have to wing it then.

Arrived at Grand Canyon depot at 11:45 - no cabs. Asked a park ranger who gave me a number for Xanterra who arrange cabs, but no service on the mobile. 20 minutes passed and we were panicking. We ran into the El Tovar and asked the concierge for help - she called Xanterra who said it would be 45 minutes…+ 20 to the airport = flight missed. She called Maverick for us and I spoke to a guy…he left me on hold a while and came back to tell me a car would be there in 9 minutes.

We arrived at the airport at 12:35, sweating! From that point we relaxed. We got weighed and bags stored. Our pilot for the day was BJ, who took us out to the helicopter for quick introductions.

There were 6 people on the flight, organised by weight. The helicopter has 2 banks of seats, with 3 available in front and 4 in rear. My wife and daughter were in the front row and I was rear left. Views were exceptional in the front seats and excellent for me in the back. Not so sure how people in the middle of rear would have found it. But it's luck of the draw. If you are light and slim, you will likely be in the front.

BJ was an entertaining and informative host and kept us all interested and engaged throughout the flight. The first 5 minutes of the flight took us over trees and scrub, towards the lip of the canyon. Then jaws literally dropped as BJ took us over the edge. Imagine sitting on a rollercoaster as it attempts its vertical drop…now imagine that drop is 6,000 feet down! What a feeling! There was significant clutching going on as fingernails gripped seats.

For the rest of the flight we navigated from south to north and back. The colours, the lines of evolution, the difference in vegetation - its not something you can easily see just walking around the rim, but up in the air the stunning vista opens up magically.

On return we found that Maverick had organised for us to share a cab back to the South Rim so we could get our return train. In summary, Maverick provided us with a genuine highlight of our holiday, rescued us from potential disaster and stopped up when they needed to. for that, it was a 5* experience.

However, I have some constructive criticism to make re the booking process:

Shuttle transport should be available to get clients from the South Rim to the airport. If you book as a package with the train company, or with Maverick airlines as part of a tour you do. As an independent booking you don't. It would take away the stress completely to know that you would be picked up and dropped off at the right time. Both trips cost us $22 + tip. I'd be happy to see this included in the overall price, just for peace of mind.

The on-line live chat team should be aware of the cab limitations from the train depot at GCSR. We were told that cabs would be readily available but on Saturday at peak time, only 3 cabs were running at one time. For the volume of visitors this seems destined for disaster. As the entire cab (and it's really a mini-bus) operation is operated by Xanterra there are no alternative options.

We highly recommend the Canyon Spirit Tour on Maverick helicopters. It gave us a fresh experience of the canyon. However, I would make sure you book either a package or have transport arranged for you before you arrive at the park.

After landing, the pilot offered to take our photos in front of the helicopter. This was well above and beyond because prior to take off, a photographer comes and takes your photo that you can purchase upon return.
Whatever this tour costs, I would HIGHLY recommend it when visiting the Grand Canyon and I would STRONGLY recommend going with Mavericks.

Review Text:
"Best hour of my life"--or at least that's how my daughter (not a little kid, but rather a highly accomplished and well travelled professional) described it. While I trust her exclamation was hyperbolic, I certainly understand her sentiments, even if I don't share her newly acquired ambition to purchase a helicopter. The Grand Canyon is vast, some 277 miles long. Short of a couple of weeks on a raft on the Colorado river, or a very very long hike, it is impossible to appreciate fully the majesty and expanse of this natural wonder other than by air. I'm a confirmed believer in enjoying landscapes slowly and under my own power and don't usually go in for this sort of thing, but the Maverick tour leaving from Tusayan left me breathless and was worth every penny (and it takes a lot of pennies to fly with Maverick). Maverick uses aircraft explicitly designed for sightseeing, which means extra glass, stadium seating, all seats facing forward and somewhat less noise and vibration (although you will certainly still need to wear the supplied noise cancelling headphones). Other companies do not necessarily use these specially purposed copters. Since all companies follow the same route, your choice basically depends on the kind of aircraft they fly and the quality of the pilot. Our pilot was tremendously knowledgeable, mixed a good deal of information with a bit of humor and made every effort to insure a pleasant and relaxed experience for all. We happened to have the great good fortune to sit in the front row of seats which undoubtedly offer a superior experience--you can request the front row, but ultimately seating is determined by the need to distribute passenger weight. We took the longer 45 minute tour (which actually lasted closer to an hour); there isn't much difference in price compared to shorter flights from Tusayan, and I can see no reason why anyone would opt for less time over the canyon, short of a fear of heights in which case they don't belong on this trip anyway. I won't attempt to describe the sights you will see, since words can not do justice to the undulating otherworldly beauty of this place. Its as simple as this: If you are going to the trouble of visiting the Grand Canyon and can afford the fare, take this flight! Economize if need be on accommodations or meals (you can eat anywhere) and take this flight! (I've spent 8 years regretting not taking a helicopter over the Na-apali coast on Kauai--avoid my folly!)
Oh, there is one negative: The staff at the terminal are unhelpful, borderline rude, our flight departed 30 minutes early, we were hustled aboard and were not informed until the last minute that you can't bring pretty much anything aboard other than a camera and a bottle of water, forcing us to make some rather hurried adjustments. (Do bring your camera rather than paying the outrageous fees they will charge you for a video of your flight or a family photo). Bottom line: Maverick ain't great on the ground, but once airborne, its a nearly transcendental experience.

Review Title: Great way to see the Grand Canyon
Review Text:
Let me start by mentioning that I have a serious fear of heights. But it has never bothered me on airplanes where I am completely enclosed.

The night before the flight (which was my first helicopter flight), we stayed at the Kachina Lodge in Grand Canyon National Park. As much is possible, I tried to stay about 6 feet away from the wall at the edge of the walkway. When I got closer, my acrophobia started to kick in. But in the helicopter, like in a plane, it didn't bother me at all.

We had five passengers on our flight, and with a helicopter that seats eight, 3+ the pilot in the front row and four in the back row, the pilot put my wife and I on the outside seats in the back row, and the other passengers in the front row with him, so everyone had a window seat and a great view. The pilot was a young guy but seemed very knowledgeable about the Grand Canyon. It was both an informative and enjoyable experience. For me, it was the highlight of our trip, which included time at the Petrified Forest, Las Vegas, Zion National Park, Bryce Canyon National Park, and Arches National Park. The flight itself lasted about 40 to 45 minutes, of course with check-in (and possibly souvenir shopping) allow maybe twice that. I highly recommend it.

Review Title: Canyon Spirit Helicopter Tour: add this to your bucket list!
Review Text:
Halfway through our 45-minute tour, our pilot, BJ, asked us to let him know as soon as he'd made it to the top of our "coolest thing ever done" list. I replied, "You hit that the second we headed over the edge of the canyon!" Truly, that moment 7 minutes into the flight when we shot off the plateau of Kaibab National Forest and the Grand Canyon opened up beneath us is something I'll never forget, not to mention the unbelievable views throughout the rest of the tour.

Maverick Helicopters offers several tours in Nevada and Arizona, and reviews of different ones are combined here on TA; make sure to focus on the reviews for the specific tour you're considering taking. My review applies only to the Canyon Spirit Helicopter Tour, which departs from the South Rim Helicopter Terminal, about 6 miles south of the Grand Canyon National Park entrance, perfect for people driving themselves.

BJ was the ideal pilot: wicked sense of humour, very proactive about sharing interesting facts about the geology of the canyon, and able to answer every question thrown at him. I noted that he was also simply amazing at taking away the nervousness of the two little girls who, along with their dad, had the front seats, and he kept them engaged with jokes and questions throughout the flight.

My father and I were fortunate to each get window seats in the back row. A window seat is a must if you plan to take decent photos (a major goal for me) as you need to put your camera right against the glass to avoid reflections. Anyone stuck in a middle rear seat would not only miss photo ops but also have quite a restricted view. Currently, Maverick offers no way to reserve a specific seat position in advance, so you pays your money and you takes your chance. Since many of the negative reviews on TA reflect unhappiness with seat assignments, I'll bet that Maverick would find plenty of takers for special flights with reduced passenger numbers that avoid the need to stick anyone in a rear middle seat—I'd certainly have paid a lot more for that guarantee. This would still allow the pilot to assign the prime seating as needed to balance weight.

Be aware too that the pilots play music throughout the flight, and since musical tastes differ, you may not be keen on their choice. I wasn't (hard rock's not my scene), but honestly the Grand Canyon was so mind-blowing that BJ could have played an album of Inuit throat singing and I probably wouldn't have minded. I'll bet you find the same.

As mementos, you can purchase a photo of yourself with the pilot taken by a Maverick staff member at the start of the flight, and a DVD of your specific tour taken by the video camera mounted underneath the chopper, which includes the audio of all cockpit conversations and the background music. You are free to take photos to your heart's content during the flight (don't forget to pack extra memory cards), but not on the ground on the helipad, for legitimate safety reasons.

Check-in was quick and friendly. They need to weigh you for weight distribution on the chopper, but this is painless as the scale is built into the floor at the check-in desk; don't worry if you're not proud of your stats, as they don't broadcast your number to the room or even mention it to you. Note that you're not allowed to bring a backpack or handbag on board, so plan accordingly. I had my camera on a shoulder strap, and that was no problem.

My 80-year-old dad was grinning ear-to-ear throughout the flight, and hasn't stopped raving about it since. This tour is absolutely worth the $274 per person charge; I give it my highest recommendation. Heartfelt thanks to BJ and the Maverick ground crew for a priceless memory.

Review Text:
If you're thinking of visiting the Grand Canyon this is not to be missed. I'm a nervous flyer so I was a little apprehensive about booking a helicopter flight but there was nothing to worry about. The initial part of the flight is over a woodland between the airport and the south rim, during this part of the flight the helicopter stays quite low to the ground which gives you time to get used to the idea of being in a helicopter before you get to the canyon edge and the once you get to the canyon there is so much to look at there isn't time to be nervous! There was also music on in the helicopter which really helped to calm my nerves. The pilot we had was named BJ and he was very chatty and helpful throughout the flight telling facts about the canyon and answering any questions we had. We took the 45 minute flight from the south rim and it was definitely a once in a lifetime experience, I don't believe there would be any better way of seeing the canyon!

Just something to remember - Arizona is an hour in front of Nevada! I know this is probably obvious to most people but being from a country which is all within 1 time zone we didn't think to check and it nearly caused us to miss our flight!

Review Text:
The flight over the Grand Canyon is one of the most amazing things I have ever done and it something that I will remember for a very long time. It is ABSOLUTLEY BRILLIANT and I would highly recommend it to anyone. If there were a list of things that you simply must do before you die, this would have to be somewhere in the top ten. Seeing the Grand Canyon from the air enables you to appreciate it in a way which is just not possible from the ground. The pilot was extremely friendly and enthusiastic, ensuring that all the passengers were eager and excited before we have even taken off, and his commentary and overall professionalism during the flight made the experience all the more enjoyable.

I took my flight from Maverick Helicopter’s base at Grand Canyon Airport, near Tusayan. They offer a pleasant waiting area and sell refreshments, t-shirts and souvenirs. The flight itself is recorded, and you have the option afterwards of buying a souvenir DVD of your own actual flight, together with a photograph of yourself standing next to the helicopter before take-off.

If you have previously taken a helicopter ride over a city, it is possible that you may have thought that it was good but not great, or that it was a lot of money to pay for quite a short experience and perhaps not worth the cost. If this is the case, do not let that put you off. Having also taken helicopter rides over cities, I can say that the Grand Canyon experience is in a completely different league, and whilst on a city flight you may get only around 15 or 20 minutes, here you get a good 40 minutes or more in the air.

The flight currently costs $275 per person (plus tip, plus cost of souvenir photo, DVD, T-shirt etc.!) A common response I had in the days immediately afterwards when raving about the trip to other people and trying to persuade them to do it was “But it is very expensive”. It is of course perfectly reasonable that any rational person will be apprehensive about spending such a large amount of money and question whether it is wise.

When it comes to this experience, my advice is this: Don’t dwell on it; if you possibly can, say to yourself ‘never mind the cost’, and just do it. Whether this is your first time in a helicopter or you have flown in one many times before, you are in for an amazing time and you will not regret it.

Review Title: One of the highlights of my holiday
Review Text:
We had booked this 45 minutes flight from the south rim before we left the UK. I am so glad that we did as the National Park was shut when we arrived there due to the Government shutdown.
The airport is easy to find, being on the main highway, and there is plenty of parking on arrival. The reception area is nice and large with a gift shop and plenty of seating area. We found the staff very friendly and helpful. What was a nice touch is that the pilot comes and calls you when he is ready to start loading the helicopter. This provides an opportunity for a chat and breaks the ice a bit. Following a brief safety chat you are taken outside to the helicopter where you have your photograph taken. These can be purchased at the end of the flight but there is no pressure to do so. The helicopters are very modern with good views from wherever you sit. Take note that seating is organised by weight to ensure the helicopter is balanced correctly. Once you get clearance you are ready to go!
The flight itself....well it was one of the most amazing trips I have ever taken. As we headed out over the National Park, the pilot pointed out all sorts of information along the way. He was witty and his commentary made the trip all the more enjoyable. Nothing any body says can prepare you for the sight of the Grand Canyon from the sky!
If you are worried about flying in a helicopter don't be, it is smoother than an aeroplane. A wonderful experience made all the more enjoyable by the effort made by Mavericks.

Review Text:
We booked the South Rim tour plus helicopter flight and we were so glad we did because we had the most amazing 5 hours. We were picked up right on time from MGM Grand and then a 20 minute ride to the smaller airport in Vegas. A quick check-in (you will need photo ID) then onto a small 16ish seater propeller plane with our 2 excellent crew - straight out of Top Gun !!
The flight to the Grand Canyon airport was about 45 minutes and all passengers were encouraged to go to the flight deck (no doors here !!) and chat to the pilots who were very happy to also take photos. After landing we were met by a small coach who took us to the canyon rim - words and photos will never do it justice - the canyon is unbelievable - and with our packed lunch (included in the price) we sat for about an hour just staring at the views. The coach then took us back to the Maverick offices close to the airport where the best was yet to come.
I have never been in a helicopter but there was no need for nerves as we smoothly took off and headed for the rim over the forest clad plateau. This was exhilerating enough but what followed as we flew across and around the Grand Canyon was incredible - I cannot put into words how fabulous it was and will never ever forget it. Back at base we then enjoyed another greta flight back to Vegas - a slightly different route with more amazing views and finally back to the hotel
If you do only 1 thing in Vegas - do this trip - worth every single cent of the price
